parts.text: Sketch a graph to show the results of this study. You must label the axes.

text: A study tested the relationship between average number of hours of sleep per night and physical
health. The participants slept in their own homes. The results showed a positive correlation.
An investigation is testing the hypothesis that, ‘intelligence affects obedience’.
State whether this is a directional or a non-directional hypothesis. Justify your answer.
In the study by Bandura et al. (aggression), a sample of children was recruited from a university
nursery. The sampling technique is not stated.
Suggest why Bandura et al. may not have used volunteer sampling.
Describe structured interviews and semi-structured interviews, using any example(s).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest two questions that Dr Jones could use in a self-report (questionnaire or interview)
that would investigate different features of Kevan’s mindfulness.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Dr Jones wants to investigate whether Kevan has changed in any ways that could be linked
to his mindfulness. He plans to interview Kevan’s friends.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest two changes in Kevan that his friends could observe. These changes must be
behavioural, emotional or cognitive.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain why one of the changes that you suggested in part (b)(i) would be difficult to
investigate.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Dr Jones has several different questions on his self-report that he has used repeatedly with a
similar case. He has identified two problems:
• Problem 1: when he studies the responses to one item, he discovers that there are
several different ways to interpret the answers.
• Problem 2: he is concerned that another item, which was supposed to measure
mindfulness, is measuring happiness instead.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain which problem relates to reliability.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain which problem relates to validity.

text: Dr Jones is conducting a case study of a man, Kevan, who has been practising mindfulness for
10 years.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain why suggestion 1 would make Dr Mohan’s study more ethical.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why suggestion 2 would make Dr Mohan’s study more ethical.

text: Dr Mohan has proposed a study using monkeys in a laboratory. A colleague has two suggestions
to make the study more ethical:
• suggestion 1: using animals which have less complex brains
• suggestion 2: using videos of the animals’ behaviour in their natural habitat.

parts.text:
Kioni is deciding how frequently throughout her participants’ lives she should test them.
Suggest a suitable frequency for Kioni to use to test her participants throughout their lives.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest one way for Kioni to re-contact her participants each time she needs to test them.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Describe one way that Kioni could measure personal space.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
For the way you described in part (c)(i):
Suggest one strength of measuring personal space in this way.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Kioni is concerned that there may be variables other than age that could affect an individual’s
personal space preferences.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Suggest two variables that could affect an individual’s preferred personal space, other
than age and gender.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
For one of the variables that you suggested in part (d)(i):
Suggest how this variable could affect an individual’s preferred personal space.

Section B

text: Kioni is conducting a longitudinal study. Her aim is to study changes in preferred personal space
throughout her participants’ lives.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how Isla could conduct an experiment to test whether attention is better if students
can play with a pen or play with an object that is not used for writing.
Do not describe sample / sampling technique or ethical issues / guidelines in your answer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: For one feature of the experiment you have described in part (a):

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Explain why that feature is a strength of the study.
Do not refer to sampling or ethics in your answer.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain how that feature could be a weakness of the study.
Do not refer to sampling or ethics in your answer.

text: Isla is a teacher. She thinks that allowing students to play with an object in class will improve
attention. Isla is unsure whether it will be better to play with a pen or play with a different object
that is not used for writing.
